chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani; al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattab, and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran (may Allah be pleased with them) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki said: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas said: 'Ubayn ibn Hisham said on the authority of 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

In His Word, the Mighty and High: (So when I have made him complete and breathed into him of My Spirit), he replied: Verily Allah, the Mighty and High, created a creation and created a spirit, then commanded an angel to breathe into him; hence it is not that which nullified any of His power.
(So when I have made him complete and breathed into him of My Spirit)
Chapter: The Negation of Place, Time, Rest, Motion, Descent, Ascent, and Transition from Allah, the Mighty and High
ai.seo_question: How does the Shia interpretation of 'breathing spirit' explain Allah's power and attributes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'breathing of spirit' into Adam signifies a distinct creation of a physical form and a separate spirit, which the angel then introduces, rather than God physically exhaling a part of His essence. This interpretation supports the Shia theological doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), affirming that God is free from physical limitations such as place, time, motion, or spatial transition, thereby preventing anthropomorphic misconceptions of the Divine.
